newsitem.title: GERMANY: German Bunds end lower, outlook unfavourable.
newsitem.headline: German Bunds end lower, outlook unfavourable.

text.p: German Bunds ended lower on Friday, dragged down by a fall in U.S. Treasuries in response to U.S. retail sales and producer prices data.
The June Bund future ended 0.24 point lower at 99.87.
Dealers said the outlook for the market for next week was negative, with poor sentiment in the U.S. market seen weighing on prices here.
But prices remained underpinned by the expectation that interest rates here will remain stable for some time, dealers said.

Dealers said Bunds may outperform U.S. Treasuries, with the spread of 10-year U.S. bonds over Bunds set to widen further. But the German market would not be able to avoid following U.S. bonds lower, the dealers said.
The spread stood at 114 at 1550 GMT, unchanged from the prior close, after a big upward revision in February U.S. retail sales to 1.5 percent from 0.8 percent.
U.S. bonds were sharply lower as investors reacted to a strong first-quarter retail sales picture and a sharper-than-expected jump in the March core Producer Price Index.
February U.S. retail sales were revised up to 1.5 percent from an originally reported 0.8 percent. The March rise in retail sales was 0.2 percent, weaker than anticipated.

The U.S. Producer Price Index fell 0.1 percent in March after dropping 0.4 percent in February and 0.3 percent percent in January. But the picture was less benign when the often-volatile food and energy sector was excluded.

This so-called core rate, which economists believe more closely tracks inflation, rose 0.4 percent after falling 0.1 percent in February. Wall Street had estimated overall prices would be unchanged while the core rate would be up 0.1 percent.
